summary: T5 ICS import UI reviewed against approved gates 00-03 and packet acceptance criteria. All 6 approved tests present and passing (19/19). canCreateEvents correctly gates owner/manager/editor with details access and !archived; editor gains no management controls. Local .ics extension and 1 MiB validation occur before any request. submitting guard prevents double-submit; all controls disabled while pending. Success shows imported_events count until Done. Safe client-owned copy for invalid_calendar_file, calendar_import_limit_exceeded, and unknown failures — no server text leaks. 401/403/404/409 route to refreshAfterAccessChange which also closes the import dialog. Escape closes the dialog and restores focus to the trigger button. CSS follows existing dialog conventions. No out-of-scope edits in the T5 files. No defects found.
important_context: Commit f8c39b9 bundles CalDAV slices 1-2 and ICS import; T5 delta is limited to CalendarManagement.tsx (+130/-2), CalendarManagement.css (+145), CalendarManagement.test.tsx (+100), and api.ts (+53 T4 contract).
Success message shows imported_events only (not imported_exceptions), matching the approved design and test expectation of '2 events imported'.
onAccessDenied prop is required by the acceptance criterion 'access denial refreshes calendars' and is not an out-of-scope addition.
Focus restoration uses useEffect cleanup on triggerEl rather than the SharingDialog parent-tracking pattern; both work correctly in tests and production.
413 and unknown HTTP failures fall through to the generic safe copy per the T4 safe-fallback contract in api.ts.
